DISCLOSURE — dual-use content declaration
=========================================

Package: dsh-redteam-mode
Declared class: dual-use (see "contentPolicy" in package.json)
Upstream: https://github.com/Jueze-2019/dsh-redteam-mode
Policy reference: https://docs.npmjs.com/policies/dual-use

What this package is
--------------------

dsh-redteam-mode is a plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) that turns the agent
runtime into an orchestration console for **authorized** adversary emulation and
penetration-testing engagements. It is an orchestration, evidence-recording and
reporting layer. Its security-relevant nature comes from what it *drives* and
*records*, not from shipping attack code.

This package contains NO exploit code
-------------------------------------

The published tarball contains no vulnerability exploits, no payloads, no
shellcode, no credential dumps and no C2 implants. It consists of:

  lib/            orchestration logic, a local SQLite fact base, tool schemas,
                  a right-side console UI and report rendering
  skills/         23 Markdown instruction documents (prose runbooks) telling an
                  agent how to *operate* third-party tools the user installs
  presets/        agent preset composition (YAML)
  scripts/        redteam-setup.sh — an optional environment bootstrap that
                  downloads well-known open-source security tools (nmap, nuclei,
                  fscan, gogo, chisel, frp, ...) into the user's own home
                  directory

Dual-use capabilities, and their legitimate use
-----------------------------------------------

1. Orchestrating security tooling. The plugin coordinates scanning tools that the
   user installs themselves and records what was found. Legitimate use: running a
   scoped, authorized assessment against systems the operator owns or has written
   permission to test.

2. Command execution on the operator's own machine. Tool invocations are issued on
   the local host that runs DSH — the operator's own assessment workstation or a
   disposable virtual machine. The package does not self-propagate, does not
   install persistence, and does not contact any server controlled by the author.

3. Reconnaissance guidance. Skills describe passive and active information
   gathering techniques. Legitimate use: mapping the attack surface of an
   authorized target, which is the standard first phase of any engagement.

4. Credential and session handling guidance. Skills describe testing for weak
   credentials on systems within an authorized scope, and how to record sessions
   the operator has legitimately obtained. All captured material stays in a local
   SQLite database under the operator's own $DSH_HOME directory; it is never
   transmitted anywhere by this package.

5. Environment bootstrap (scripts/redteam-setup.sh). This shell script downloads
   open-source security binaries from their official GitHub release assets into
   $DSH_HOME/redteam/toolkit/. It does not install system packages, does not
   require or use sudo, does not modify network or proxy configuration, and does
   not run any downloaded binary beyond a --version/-h smoke test. Operators who
   prefer to install these tools themselves can skip the script entirely; nothing
   in the plugin requires it to run.

Hard boundaries the package declares and enforces
-------------------------------------------------

* Authorization-only. The README, the agent preset and all role prompts state that
  use is limited to engagements with written authorization, and that unauthorized
  scanning or intrusion is illegal in most jurisdictions.
* Local-only data. No telemetry, no analytics, no cloud sync, no author-controlled
  endpoints. All findings stay on the operator's machine.
* Judgement-free tooling. The package does not decide whether a target is in scope;
  that determination is the operator's responsibility.

Intended operators
------------------

Professional penetration testers, red teams and security engineers running
authorized engagements, typically inside a dedicated and disposable Kali virtual
machine rather than on a day-to-day workstation.
